decisions.reason: As a close extension of the core offer, the fifteen-day express program is likely to stay because its fit with existing operations and the firm's slack outweigh the limited signal of only modest market prominence.

The seventy-two-hour express program faces the highest discontinuation risk because its extreme service promise is operationally costly and may fall short of aspiration levels if demand or margins disappoint, but a large firm in a growing market will still likely give it more time.

The fire-resistant steel exterior door is strongly aligned with the firm's safety-focused core business and its prominent launch with European approval suggests performance expectations are likely being met or are worth supporting further.

The express delivery program for doors and gates is close to the established business and its dedicated page indicates managerial commitment, so it is likely to be retained unless results clearly miss aspirations.

The online ordering and digital services platform supports the firm's broader move toward advisory and service integration, and a large firm with development resources is likely to continue it despite early adoption uncertainty.

The fire and smoke protection door fits the firm's compliance and safety strengths, and even with only limited website prominence it is likely to be kept because it uses existing capabilities and serves stable customer needs.
